$comment: Which lane the leader dispatches for each kind of work. A lane is a runner plus a model. Read it through the route script, never by hand. Changed only through a pull request.

leader.rule: The leader's own login runs no tasks and is never in a rotation.

notes: Opus 5.5 can end an unattended turn with a progress note and no result; when a run stops that way, send "continue" on the same thread before you count it as done.
Give Terra explicit allowed actions, never conditions.

globalBans.rule: A review, re-check or QA runs on a different model from the one that wrote the work.
A lane with local: true is in no row with writes: true.
What a pi lane wrote merges only after a review on a Claude lane.
A risk-high change is reviewed by a different vendor from its author when a lane of one has budget, and never on the author's login.
A lane with enforcesToolLimits: false is in no reading row (writes: false and not runsCode) and in no security-and-release row.

tieRule: When two rows match, a row that narrows the other wins. Otherwise the lookAlike rule for the pair decides. When no rule decides, follow noMatch.

noMatch.rule: When no row matches, ask the owner. When unattended, park the task in parked.md and dispatch nothing.

lookAlikes.rule: scoped-recheck judges whether a finding is fixed; review-response-one changes code to answer a verdict.
A PR that conflicts with its base is conflict-repair until the resolution is pushed to its branch; landing it afterwards is merge-chain.
lookAlikes.test: A merge chain stopped on a conflict in two files hands that PR to conflict-repair, which pushes the resolution to the PR branch; merge-chain then lands it.

lookAlikes.rule: A picture that must be invented is generated-images; a figure that must be correct is diagrams.

ux-design decides how a surface is used and comes first; ui-design decides how it looks, on a landed flow; design-system changes what every design is built from. A new component inside a feature is two tasks: design-system, then ui-design.
refactor restructures product code with no behaviour change; kit-refactor changes the pipeline's own tooling.
ui-tests writes a suite that runs again tomorrow; browser-qa runs this change once and judges it; evidence-pass collects what already happened.
lookAlikes.test: "Test the UI" is browser-qa when it means this change, and ui-tests when it means from now on.

lookAlikes.rule: design-review judges a screen against the design; browser-qa judges whether the change works.
ui-design writes design files and no product code; ui-implementation writes the product code that matches them.
lookAlikes.test: "Make it look right" is ui-design when no design says what right is, and ui-implementation when one does.

lookAlikes.rule: Changing what a screen says in its current language is ui-implementation; making text translatable or adding a listed language is localisation.
browser-qa asks whether the change works and broke nothing; acceptance-verification checks each accepted criterion of the issue.
analysis plans one feature; architecture-decision binds the next ten; spike is for when nobody can decide yet, because nobody knows.
Each needs its own go from the owner; none implies another.
bounded-bug-fix when the failing test and the file are known; diagnose-bug when the cause still has to be found; hotfix when people hit the fault right now.
lookAlikes.test: "Fix this crash" is diagnose-bug until someone can name the file and write a failing test.

lookAlikes.rule: unit-tests prove one part alone with fakes; integration-tests prove two real parts together; regression-suite curates the tests that pin past bugs.
lookAlikes.test: "Add tests for the parser" is unit-tests; "test the parser against the real files on disk" is integration-tests.

rows.title: Spike: one open technical question, answered by trying
rows.trigger: Somebody cannot decide until they know whether something is possible, how hard it is or how it behaves, and the way to find out is to try it.

rows.title: Deprecation plan
rows.trigger: Something people depend on has to be retired, and nothing may be removed until who is affected, the replacement and the dates are written down.

rows.title: Dependency maintenance

rows.title: Hotfix: a live fault, the narrowest fix now
rows.trigger: People are hitting the fault right now, and waiting for the full fix costs more than shipping a narrow one and following up.

rows.title: Refactor: structure changes, behaviour does not
rows.trigger: The product's code has to be restructured and nothing a user or a caller can observe may change.
notes: Never a single mid lane with no review.

rows.title: Migration: data, a schema or a format changes shape
rows.trigger: Something that already exists outside the code (rows, files, a config people wrote by hand) has to move to a new shape.

rows.title: Observability: logs, metrics, alerts, runbooks
rows.trigger: People cannot tell what a part of the system is doing, and the change adds signals and changes no behaviour.

rows.title: Localisation: translatable text, a listed locale
rows.trigger: Text has to become translatable, or a language the owner has listed has to be added or brought up to date.

never.why: owner's preference

rows.title: Automated UI tests: built or maintained
rows.trigger: A user-visible behaviour has to be protected by a test that drives the real interface in a browser, again and again, with nobody watching.

never.why: owner's preference

rows.title: Unit tests for one part on its own
rows.trigger: The job is tests for one function, module or class with its collaborators faked, and no product behaviour changes.
notes: A pi write opens a draft PR that needs a full Claude review.

rows.title: Integration tests: two real parts across a boundary
rows.trigger: The thing to prove is that two parts work together (a handler and its database, a client and an API, a command and the file system), not that one part works alone.

rows.title: Regression suite: curated
rows.trigger: The job is the suite that pins past bugs: fixes with no test that fails without them, tests that guard nothing, or a test to retire.

rows.title: Performance and load: measured against a budget
rows.trigger: The question is whether something is fast enough, and the owner has stated the budget it answers to.
notes: Never on a shared or noisy machine. A load claim is verified only by running two specs in one suite invocation, never by a synthetic busy loop.
